title: silverline-telecom-edge-throttle-field-notes
content:
Quick capture from 2025-02-17 call with Silverline Telecom (ops/edge infra) — messy notes + action items. Notes to self: follow up on HSM timelines and whether they can accept our private control plane (they said maybe).

Attendees:
- Silverline: Nisha Rao (CTO), Omar Patel (Edge infra lead), Leena Park (SRE), Jason Wu (Product)
- Redwood: Priya (SE, owner), Diego (runtime), Alyssa (security pre-sales)

Context / TL;DR:
Silverline wants to run a conversational assistant on regional edge POPs to avoid central egress and meet local latency requirements for field technicians. Primary ask: private deploy (VPC or on-prem-like) with low-latency inference for short support flows. They are sensitive about any traffic leaving region and want token-level billing/visibility. Budget uncertain; want a pilot first.

Primary non-functional requirements (as stated):
- P95 latency target: <= 140ms for 64-token generation (target use is short completions)
- Cold-start for a single request (no warm KV) ideally < 250ms
- Sustained concurrency expected: 60 concurrent sessions per POP (peak), avg request rate 18 RPS per POP, burst to 120 RPS for short windows during shift change
- Deployment constraints: edge POPs are AWS Outposts-like boxes (4x A30-ish), limited storage (1.2TB), constrained egress (policy: no model weights may leave customer-controlled storage)
- Security/compliance: KMS required for root keys, prefer HSM for token signing, audit logs retained locally for 90 days only
- Observability: must support per-route latency and token counts, and stream traces to their Splunk instance over private peering

Functional notes / product asks:
- Streaming support is important (they want progressive answers on mobile clients). Must support chunked HTTP/WS streaming with the same token-level metering output.
- Tools/function-calling: they want ability to call internal probes (e.g., device-status-check) during the chat, so Redwood function-calling is relevant. Need mapping for service discovery behind private network.
- Model: they will test with a small open LLM (quantized fp16 -> int8 recommended by Diego). They want a fallback lighter model if heavy load detected.

Gotchas / red flags flagged on call:
1) "No weights leaving our S3" policy — means we cannot pull from Redwood-managed model store. Need to support bringing-your-own-model (BYOM) with offline model import and local packaging. Action: confirm BYOM import flow + checksum validation.
2) HSM integration timeline unclear — they said HSM procurement could be 6-8 weeks. Our KMS/HSM adapters may need to be turned on later in pilot. Workaround: use customer KMS (software) initially, with limited scope. Note: Alyssa to confirm security acceptance criteria.
3) Edge GPU memory constraint — 4x A30 with mixed workloads could cause KV cache thrashing if we use large context. Need to recommend short context windows (512 tokens) and aggressive KV eviction policy. Diego suggests we test with dynamic batching and early flush on long-tail sessions.
4) Networking: private peering to Splunk only, no external metrics egress. Our default hosted metrics collector will not work. We must ship metrics via forwarder container running on their network. Ops note: ensure metrics plugin supports TLS mutual auth and their CA.
5) Token-level accounting: they want same granularity as hosted API. We need to expose per-session token counters and logs locally — confirm retention and legal review.

Initial architecture sketch (informal):
- Private control plane with customer subnet for model artifacts (S3-like). Redwood agent in POP for model load, runtime on k8s nodepool pinned to GPU nodes.
- Model packaging: customer uploads quantized model tar to their S3; Redwood agent validates and mounts to local path. No outbound model download.
- Metrics: local Prom + push gateway -> secure forwarder -> Splunk HEC (private peering).
- Fallback: small 4-bit quantized variant on same nodes; routing policy by queue depth.

Technical tests to run in POC (prioritized):
1) Cold-start latency test (single request to empty node) — target < 250ms
2) Steady-state p95 with synthetic 18 RPS/multi-session mix for 512-token context (target <= 140ms)
3) Burst handling: ramp to 120 RPS for 30s windows, observe queue latency and tail – measure degrade curve
4) Streaming correctness + token-metering parity vs hosted API (compare counts for identical prompts)
5) Model-import validation: integrity check, load time, memory usage, model shard mapping (if we need model sharding)

Open questions (need answers from Silverline):
- Can we use CPU-only agents for control-plane tasks (yes likely) or must everything run on GPU nodes?
- Precise Splunk HEC endpoint + certs (Omar to provide by next week)
- Legal: acceptable data residency wording and retention policy for logs (Jason to loop legal)
- SLA expectations for pilot vs production (they keep shifting between low-latency promise and cost limits)

Immediate next steps (owner tags):
- Priya: Draft SOW for 6-week pilot; include BYOM import, 3 POPs, metrics forwarder, support hours. Target to share by 2025-02-21.
- Diego: Prototype quantized load on dev-box (A30) with 512 token profile; capture p95 baseline and memory map. Deliver artifact + perf notes by 2025-02-24.
- Alyssa: Security checklist for initial non-HSM KMS setup + list of controls to require before pilot. Due 2025-02-20.
- Omar (customer): Provide Splunk endpoint + cert + sample S3 bucket for model upload by 2025-02-25.
- Marcus (Redwood ops): Draft metrics forwarder container spec and mutual TLS sample config by 2025-02-22.

Notes to self / friction points to watch:
- If they insist on no telemetry leaving network, we may lose some product analytics; record tradeoffs in SOW.
- Quantization mismatch between their toolchain and our runtime could require a conversion step. Factor ~2 days for a conversion script in POC.
- Prepare a short demo script that shows graceful degrade to fallback model and streaming tokens — sells really well to product folks.

Meeting cadence: weekly sync (Tues 10am PT) for duration of pilot. Next meeting scheduled: 2025-02-25 10:00 PT.

Random scratch / brainstorm (unstructured):
- Could offer a "local observability bundle" (container + preconfigured dashboards + forwarder) as pilot add-on — upsell path for production.
- Consider an offline model package validator we can ship (lambda-like) to run in their network if they demand no outbound connections. Could be a small binary that performs integrity checks + outputs manifest.

End of notes. Will tidy and convert into SOW draft later.
